Steps: 1. Check your interior mirror for what is behind you. 2. Check the door mirror on the side you are moving to. 3. Signal in good time. 4. Take a quick glance over your shoulder to clear the blind spot. 5. Move across smoothly in one steady movement. 6. Cancel the signal and settle into the new lane.
Callout: One lane at a time. Never two at once.

Steps: 1. Slow down early and get into the correct position. 2. Signal right in good time. 3. Check your mirrors and the road you are turning into. 4. Take the turn at a speed that lets you stay in your own lane. 5. Straighten up and build speed gently once you are round.

1. Begin slowing well before the junction. 2. Move to the correct position near the centre line. 3. Signal left across the oncoming lane in good time. 4. Stop at the give-way line if you cannot see a clear gap. 5. Watch the oncoming traffic and judge the gaps, not the cars. 6. Look through the turn to where you want to end up. 7. Check for pedestrians crossing the road you are entering. 8. Wait for a gap you are certain of, not one you are hoping for. 9. When the gap is clear, turn smoothly across the lane. 10. Keep your wheels straight while you wait so a knock will not push you forward. 11. Complete the turn into your own lane and cancel the signal.
Callout: When in doubt, wait. A missed gap costs seconds; a wrong one costs more.

Steps: 1. Read the signs and road markings on the approach. 2. Slow down early and choose your lane before you arrive. 3. Give way to traffic already on the roundabout, usually from your left. 4. Wait for a gap and enter without stopping if you can. 5. Keep to your lane and follow the markings round. 6. Signal left as you pass the exit before the one you want. 7. Leave the roundabout in your lane and check your mirror.
Callout: Look left, take your time, and keep moving when it is clear.

Steps: 1. Find a space at least a car and a half long. 2. Pull up level with the car in front, about half a metre out. 3. Check your mirrors and blind spot for anything coming. 4. Select reverse and begin backing slowly. 5. When your back wheels are level with the other car's bumper, turn the wheel toward the kerb. 6. Bring the car back at a shallow angle. 7. When the front clears the parked car, straighten the wheel. 8. Reverse gently until you are parallel with the kerb. 9. Adjust forward and back until you are centred in the space.
Callout: Slow and small. Let the wheel do the work.

Steps: 1. Build your speed along the slip road to match the traffic. 2. Check your mirrors as you go. 3. Look for a gap in the lane you are joining. 4. Signal to show where you are going. 5. Keep glancing between the road ahead and your mirror. 6. Ease into the gap at matching speed. 7. Do not stop on the slip road unless you have to. 8. Cancel your signal and keep a safe distance.
Callout: Match the speed, find the gap, ease in.

Steps: 1. Come to a full stop at the line, every time. 2. The first vehicle to stop is the first to go. 3. If two of you arrive together, the one on the right goes first. 4. When it is your turn, move off clearly so others know.
Callout: Full stop, then first come, first go.

Steps: 1. Keep scanning far ahead, not just the car in front. 2. Ask what could happen next and cover the brake. 3. Slow down before a hazard, not on top of it.
Callout: See it early, and you have time.
